summary: Sprint 3 retrospective: the team delivered tested JWT authentication and task isolation, while security identified an unresolved login timing-enumeration mitigation.

messages.content: The retrospective records the unresolved login timing-enumeration mitigation; complete it under the existing be-3 work before security sign-off.

blockers: Security sign-off remains blocked until login executes equivalent password-derivation work for unknown and known usernames.
decisions: Retrospective dialogue: Architect: “I confirmed the standard-library JWT contract and ownership boundary before implementation.” Database: “The user and task-ownership migration preserved legacy tasks while making authenticated queries user-scoped.” Backend: “I delivered registration, login, HS256 Bearer validation, and per-user task enforcement.” Frontend: “I completed sign-in, registration, session-scoped token storage, and 401 recovery, and kept the editor open on failed saves.” QA: “Four passing regressions covered auth, password storage, protected CRUD, user isolation, token rejection, and frontend integration markers.” Security: “The core controls checked out, but login returns early for unknown users and needs equalized PBKDF work to avoid a timing distinction.” Manager: “The implementation and QA handoffs completed; the sprint cannot receive final security sign-off until the existing backend task addresses that finding.”
